docs.title: System Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The system operates securely inside the Lion International Bank Private Intranet / Domain, isolated behind corporate network perimeters. Dynamic requests are routed via an Nginx reverse proxy to the Frappe Framework / Python WSGI application container, heavy computations are decoupled using Redis Queue (RQ) background workers, and persistent data is stored in MariaDB Enterprise alongside a native Ethiopian Calendar (EC \(\leftrightarrow\) GC) translation engine.

docs.title: Lion International Bank Human Resource & Integrated Payroll Management System (anbesa_hr)
1. Architectural Overview & Context
docs.text:
The Lion International Bank HRMS (anbesa_hr) is architected as a secure, multi-tier, modular enterprise application hosted entirely on Ubuntu Linux within the Lion International Bank Private Intranet / Domain.

The architecture strictly separates: 1. User Access & Role Boundaries: Segregates General Staff (ESS), Branch Managers (MSS), HR Operations, and System Admins. 2. Perimeter Ingress & Security: Nginx acts as the reverse proxy, terminates SSL/TLS, and serves static assets directly. 3. Application & Business Logic: Frappe Framework hosting the custom anbesa_hr banking app and standard HRMS modules. 4. Asynchronous Background Processing: Decouples heavy operations (payroll calculations, report compiling) using Redis Queue (RQ) and background workers to prevent web interface timeouts. 5. Persistence & Localization: MariaDB relational database paired with the native Ethiopian Calendar (EC \(\leftrightarrow\) GC) translation engine. 6. Downstream Banking Operations: Decoupled file-based integration producing standardized Core Banking System (CBS) disbursement files (CSV/Excel) for salary credit, with direct API integration and biometric attendance scheduled for Phase 2.

docs.title: Layer 1: Bank Users & Access Layer
docs.text:
• Employee Self-Service (ESS): All branch and head office staff access payslips, leave balances, leave applications, and self-evaluations.
  • Branch & Line Managers (MSS): Approves leave requests for team members, conducts annual appraisals, and endorses temporary acting appointments.
  • HR Operations & Payroll Specialists: Full administrative access to the employee lifecycle (recruitment, transfers, promotions, disciplinary records, guarantor files) and monthly payroll processing.
  • System Administrator & Auditor: Configures Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), manages Ethiopian calendar holidays, and inspects system audit logs.

docs.title: Layer 2: Network Perimeter & Web Gateway (Ubuntu / Nginx)
docs.text:
• Hosting Perimeter: Deployed on an Ubuntu Linux server strictly located within the Bank's Private Intranet / Domain. Access is restricted by firewall to Lion International Bank's internal IP ranges.
  • Nginx Reverse Proxy:
  • Handles standard web ports (80 / 443 HTTPS with corporate SSL certificate).
  • Serves static content (CSS, JS libraries, employee photos) directly from the disk cache.
  • Forwards dynamic requests to the Frappe application runtime on port 8000.

docs.title: Layer 3: Core Application Container (anbesa_hr on Frappe)
docs.text:
• Application Framework: Frappe Framework (Python WSGI) providing out-of-the-box user management, document state machines, and REST APIs.
  • Integrated Modules:
  • Core HR (anbesa_hr): Full 9-tab employee dossier, Ethiopian 4-tier address hierarchy (Region \(\rightarrow\) Zone \(\rightarrow\) Woreda \(\rightarrow\) Kebele), guarantor & collateral records, inter-branch transfer history, and exit clearance tracking.
  • Leave Management: Annual, sick, maternity, and exam leave allocations with dual-calendar tracking and monetary Birr encashment calculations.
  • Payroll Management: Lion International Bank salary scales, tax brackets, pension, provident fund, and monthly salary reconciliation.
  • Performance Appraisal: Current vs. future state appraisal workflows, KRA/KPI evaluation scorecards, and manager reviews.
  • Training History & Development: Registry of academic milestones, internal/external bank certifications, and employee bonding agreements.

docs.title: Layer 4: Caching & Asynchronous Queue Layer (Redis & RQ)
docs.text:
• Redis Cache: Retains user sessions, security permissions, and frequently read system settings in RAM memory, preventing repetitive database reads.
  • Redis Queue (RQ): When HR clicks "Process Monthly Payroll for 3,500 Employees", the task is placed into the background queue.
  • Background Worker: A background Python worker processes the payroll batch asynchronously without freezing the web interface or blocking other bank users.

docs.title: Layer 5: Data Persistence & Localization
docs.text:
• MariaDB Enterprise: Fully relational ACID-compliant database storing all employee records, historical salary adjustments, audit trails, and transactional records.
  • Ethiopian Calendar Engine: Bidirectional conversion logic converting Ethiopian Calendar (EC) dates (e.g., Meskerem 1, Hamle 1 – Sene 30 fiscal year) to Gregorian Calendar (GC) database timestamps.
  • Protected Media Store: Encrypted local storage on disk for employee dossier photographs, scanned guarantor undertaking forms, and clearance sign-offs.

docs.title: Layer 6: Downstream Banking & Future Expansion
docs.text:
• Phase 1 Production Flow (File-Based Export):
  • The system does not perform direct automated API posts to Core Banking yet.
  • At the end of each payroll cycle, the system generates a standardized Core Banking Salary Disbursement Batch File (CSV / Excel format) detailing: $\(\text{Employee Account Number} \quad|\quad \text{Employee Name} \quad|\quad \text{Branch Code} \quad|\quad \text{Net Salary (ETB)} \quad|\quad \text{Narration}\)$
  • Finance Officers upload this file into the Bank's Core Banking System (e.g., Temenos T24 / Finacle) to disburse funds.
  • Phase 2 Expansion (Roadmap):
  • Direct CBS REST API Integration: Real-time automated salary posting via bank enterprise service bus (ESB) or API gateway.
  • Branch Biometric Attendance: Automated polling from physical fingerprint/facial recognition hardware installed across branch locations.

docs.title: 4. Technical Footprint & Infrastructure Specification
docs.text: Attribute Specification Justification Operating System Ubuntu Server 22.04 / 24.04 LTS Standard, LTS-supported, secure enterprise Linux host Network Location Bank Private LAN / Intranet (No Public IP) High security; banking employee data never leaves internal perimeter Web Gateway / Proxy Nginx 1.24+ High-concurrency reverse proxy, SSL termination, static asset acceleration Application Runtime Python 3.10+ / Gunicorn (Frappe Bench) Robust enterprise web application environment Custom App Namespace anbesa_hr (frappe-bench/apps/anbesa_hr) Houses Lion International Bank specific customizations and banking doctypes Caching & Message Broker Redis 7.x (Cache & Queue instances) Separates synchronous web traffic from bulk batch jobs (payroll/reports) Database Server MariaDB 10.6+ Enterprise Relational integrity, transactional security, audit-friendly Calendar Engine Native Python / JS Geez-Gregorian Library Supports Ethiopian fiscal year, holiday calendars, and tenure calculations Downstream Disbursal Export: Formatted Excel / CSV Batch File Safe, decoupled Maker-Checker procedure for Core Banking upload

docs.title: Lion International Bank Human Resource & Integrated Payroll Management System (anbesa_hr)
1. Purpose & Architectural Context
docs.text:
If the High-Level System Architecture (HLSA) provided the 30,000-foot view of the hosting infrastructure and bank network perimeters, this Module / Component Diagram (C4 Level 3) zooms directly into Layer 3 (The Core Application Container).

It decomposes the system into its 5 functional business subsystems, documenting: 1. Internal Components & DocTypes: The specific records, business objects, and data structures inside each module. 2. Business Controllers & Calculation Logic: The internal validation hooks, formula engines, and workflow state machines. 3. Inter-Module Data Dependencies: How data moves across module boundaries (e.g., how Leave balances flow into Payroll deductions, and how Appraisal scores trigger Salary Step Increments). 4. Cross-Cutting Utilities: Shared services like the Ethiopian Calendar (EC \(\leftrightarrow\) GC) engine and the secure document repository.

docs.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) & Maker-Checker Governance Matrix
Lion International Bank Human Resource & Integrated Payroll Management System (anbesa_hr)
1. Executive Summary & Banking Governance Principles
docs.text:
In commercial banking, access control is governed by strict compliance mandates from the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE), external auditors, and internal risk management policies.

The security architecture of LIBHRMS (anbesa_hr) is built on three core pillars: 1. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Privileges are assigned to roles, never individual users. All bank users inherit the base Employee role, while administrative privileges are additive. 2. Segregation of Duties (SoD) & Maker-Checker Principle: High-risk transactions (salary scale adjustments, promotions, disciplinary terminations, and monthly payroll disbursement) cannot be executed by a single individual. The person who drafts a transaction (The Maker) can never be the person who finalizes and authorizes it (The Checker). 3. Branch-Level Data Isolation (Row-Level Security): Branch Managers and local supervisors are restricted via Frappe User Permissions to view and act upon only employees assigned to their specific Branch / Department. Head Office HR and Finance maintain bank-wide visibility.

docs.text:
In Lion International Bank S.C. (LIB), an employee's lifecycle is governed by strict commercial banking controls and Ethiopian Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019.

This revised workflow incorporates the verified operational realities of the bank: 1. Onboarding & Master Dossier: Bilingual data capture (English and Amharic script), 4-tier Ethiopian address hierarchy (Region \(\rightarrow\) Zone \(\rightarrow\) Woreda \(\rightarrow\) Kebele), and assignment to one of three employee classes (Managerial, Clerical / Professional, Non-Clerical). 2. Confirmation to Permanent status strictly requires verified Personal Guarantors and signed liability undertaking letters recorded in employee_guarantor. 3. Career Progression & Operational Movements: Inter-branch lateral transfers, acting appointments with allowances, and performance-driven promotions. 4. Separation & Final Settlement (Labour Proclamation 1156/2019): * The 4-Point Clearance Checklist: Pragmatic checklist verified by the HR Termination Officer (Branch cash/keys, IT accounts, Finance loans, Property ID badge) without over-extending system logins. * Solving the 2-Week Leave Archive Pain Point: Replaces the manual paper archive and broken Excel spreadsheet reconciliation with instant 1-second Leave Ledger calculation (Positive balance \(\rightarrow\) Taxable Earning; Negative balance \(\rightarrow\) Wage Recovery Deduction). * Statutory Severance Pay Automation: Enforces Proclamation 1156/2019 rules (\(< 5\) years service = 0 ETB severance; \(\ge 5\) years service = statutory formula). * Automated Certificate of Service & Guarantor Release: One-click legal letter generation.

docs.title: Lion International Bank Human Resource & Integrated Payroll Management System (anbesa_hr)
1. Process Overview & Banking Context
docs.text:
In a commercial banking institution, leave management is not simply an attendance tracker—it directly impacts branch cash operations, customer service continuity, and financial liabilities.

The Leave Management Subsystem in LIBHRMS (anbesa_hr) addresses four critical banking requirements: 1. Statutory Seniority-Based Accrual: Automatic calculation of annual leave entitlements based on Ethiopian Labor Law and Lion International Bank policy: $\(\text{Annual Leave Entitlement} = 16 \text{ Days (Base)} + \left\lfloor\frac{\text{Years of Banking Service}}{2}\right\rfloor \text{ Days}\)$ 2. Reliever Handover Endorsement: A branch teller, cashier, or branch manager cannot depart on leave without formally designating an authorized Reliever who signs off on accepting the cash drawer, safe keys, and customer portfolio. 3. Dual-Calendar & Holiday Synchronization: Tracking applications across both the Gregorian Calendar (GC) and the Ethiopian Calendar (EC), excluding official national and religious public holidays automatically. 4. Monetary Leave Encashment (Birr Valuation): Converting unused accumulated leave into cash payments during separation or authorized encashment cycles, feeding taxable earnings directly into the monthly payroll slip: $\(\text{Leave Encashment (ETB)} = \left(\frac{\text{Monthly Base Salary}}{30}\right) \times \text{Encashable Days}\)$

docs.title: Stage 1: Fiscal Year Leave Allocation & Entitlement
docs.text:
• Timing: Executes at the commencement of each Ethiopian Fiscal Year (Hamle 1).
  • Automatic Seniority Computation: The system calculates total months of service at Lion International Bank.
  • Allocation Posting: Creates immutable credit entries in Leave Ledger Entry for each active staff member across statutory leave categories (Annual, Sick, Maternity, Paternity, Compassionate, Exam).

docs.title: Stage 2: Application & Reliever Handover
docs.text:
• Self-Service Application (ESS): The employee selects the leave category and specifies dates in either Gregorian (GC) or Ethiopian (EC) format.
  • Mandatory Reliever Designation: In a commercial bank, no teller or manager can take leave without naming a Reliever. The system prompts for a colleague in the same branch/unit who will assume the teller stamp, cash drawer, and client duties.
  • Pre-Submission Balance Check: If requested working days exceed current remaining balance, the system halts submission immediately.

docs.title: Stage 3: Multi-Tier Supervisory Approval
docs.text:
1. Reliever Sign-Off: The designated colleague receives an inbox alert to accept or reject the handover.
  2. Branch / Line Manager Approval (MSS): The branch manager verifies branch staffing coverage and signs off.
  3. HR Operations Verification: HR ensures the application complies with bank-wide policies and public holiday calendars.
  4. Final Submission: The document transitions to Submitted (docstatus = 1).

docs.title: Stage 4: Ledger Debit & Operational Execution
docs.text:
• Debit Entry: Automatically generates an immutable debit transaction in the Leave Ledger Entry.
  • Dynamic Balance Update: Updates the employee's current real-time remaining balance.
  • Desk & Email Alerts: Employee and Branch Manager receive formal digital approval notices.

docs.title: Stage 5: Financial Integration & Payroll Reconciliation
docs.text:
• Standard Paid Leave: Normal annual, sick, or maternity leave has zero negative impact on monthly pay.
  • Leave Without Pay (LWP): Unpaid leave days automatically flow to the Payroll Calculation Engine, deducting daily base wages from the monthly salary slip.
  • Unused Leave Birr Encashment:
  • Triggered during annual policy encashment windows or upon employee exit.
  • Valued using the daily wage formula: \(\text{Daily Base Rate} = \frac{\text{Base Salary}}{30}\).
  • Subject to Ethiopian Personal Income Tax (PIT) and added to the employee's monthly pay slip.

1. Process Overview & Banking Context
docs.text:
In commercial banking, payroll processing is a mission-critical financial operation subject to strict internal controls, General Ledger (GL) reconciliation, and regulatory audits by the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) and the Ministry of Revenues (ERCA).

The Payroll Subsystem in LIBHRMS (anbesa_hr) governs the complete cycle: 1. Multi-Source Input Collation: Merging base salary scale assignments with monthly dynamic inputs (unpaid leave days, approved leave encashments, acting allowances, teller cash indemnity, and staff loan amortization schedules). 2. Asynchronous Batch Execution: Utilizing Redis Queue (RQ) background workers to process thousands of branch employees simultaneously without freezing the web interface. 3. Statutory & Institutional Deductions: * Ethiopian Personal Income Tax (PIT): Progressive marginal brackets (0% up to 35%). * Mandatory Pension: 7% Employee contribution, 11% Lion International Bank contribution. * Internal Deductions: Staff mortgage/consumer loan deductions, provident fund, and disciplinary cash recovery. 4. Variance Analysis & Maker-Checker Authorization: Comparing current-month payroll against the previous month, isolating discrepancies (new hires, promotions, exits), and securing Finance Director sign-off. 5. Decoupled Core Banking Handover: Generating the standardized CBS Salary Batch Export File (CSV/Excel) formatted with account numbers and net ETB amounts for manual upload and automated crediting via Core Banking.

docs.title: Stage 1: Monthly Input Collation & Cutoff
docs.text:
• The Cutoff Gate: Scheduled monthly (e.g., the 20th of the calendar month), freezing new operational adjustments to stabilize the calculation base.
  • Aggregated Inputs:
  • Core HR Master: Active employees, branch codes, salary scale step updates, promotions, and separated employees (excluded).
  • Leave Subsystem: Leave Without Pay (LWP) days (for daily wage deductions) and approved leave encashments.
  • Banking Allowances: Cashier Cash Indemnity Allowance, Acting Allowance for vacant managerial posts, and Transport/Representation.
  • Finance Loan Schedule: Amortization principal and interest repayments for staff consumer and mortgage loans.

docs.title: Stage 2: Asynchronous Batch Calculation (Redis Queue)
docs.text:
• The Scale Challenge: Calculating tax brackets, pension, loan cuts, and allowances across 3,500+ employees simultaneously takes considerable processing power.
  • The Technical Solution: The Payroll Entry dispatches the batch calculation to Redis Queue (RQ). Background Python workers execute the mathematical operations in parallel, keeping the web interface completely responsive.

docs.title: Stage 3: Statutory & Institutional Deductions Engine
docs.text:
1. Gross Earnings Formula: $\(\text{Gross Pay} = \text{Base Salary} + \text{Allowances} + \text{Leave Encashment} - \left(\frac{\text{Base Salary}}{30} \times \text{LWP Days}\right)\)$
  2. Statutory Taxes & Pension (Ethiopian Proclamation):
  3. Taxable Income: Computed after exempt allowance thresholds.
  4. Personal Income Tax (PIT): Progressive rate brackets (\(0\% \rightarrow 10\% \rightarrow 15\% \rightarrow 20\% \rightarrow 25\% \rightarrow 30\% \rightarrow 35\%\)).
  5. Pension Scheme:
    • Employee Contribution: \(7\%\) of Base Salary (deducted from gross pay).
    • Bank Contribution: \(11\%\) of Base Salary (booked as bank operational expense).
  6. Institutional Banking Deductions:
  7. Monthly staff loan deductions.
  8. Staff Provident Fund deductions.
  9. Branch cashier cash shortage deductions (disciplinary recovery).

docs.title: Stage 4: Variance Reconciliation & Maker-Checker Audit Sign-Off
docs.text:
• Variance Analysis: The system generates a comparative delta sheet comparing Month \(N\) vs. Month \(N-1\). Discrepancies (net pay changes \(> 5\%\), new joiners, leavers, grade jumps) must be reconciled by the Payroll Officer.
  • Maker-Checker Sign-Off:
  • Maker (Payroll Officer): Submits draft reconciliation.
  • Checker (Finance Director): Verifies total funding against bank General Ledger (GL) cash reserves and formally submits (docstatus = 1), making the payroll batch immutable.

Customized with Lion International Bank Appraisal Rules & Amharic Localization
1. Executive Modernization Rationale
docs.text:
In Lion International Bank S.C. (LIB), performance evaluation governs staff motivation, annual bonus distribution, and internal career promotions.

This updated specification incorporates the bank's exact operational structure: 1. Three Distinct Employee Categories & Appraisal Cycles: * Managerial: Evaluated Once a year (June 1 – Nov 30); evaluated on 15 criteria (11 base + 4 managerial leadership questions). * Clerical / Professional (Permanent staff > 45 days): Evaluated Twice a year (Cycle 1: June 1 – Nov 30, Cycle 2: Dec 1 – May 31); evaluated on 11 standard criteria. * Non-Clerical (Drivers, Janitors, Security, Messengers): Evaluated Twice a year (Cycle 1: June 1 – Nov 30, Cycle 2: Dec 1 – May 31); evaluated on 14 specific criteria 100% rendered in Amharic (Ge'ez script). 2. Standard 1 to 5 Rating Scale: * \(1 = \text{Poor}\), \(2 = \text{Satisfactory/Fair}\), \(3 = \text{Good}\), \(4 = \text{Very Good}\), \(5 = \text{Excellent}\). 3. Discrete Banking Score Conversion Bands (Average Score out of 5): * Average \(\ge 4.0\): Scored as \(100\%\) (Full performance rating / maximum bonus tier). * Average \(3.5 – 3.9\): Scored as \(75\%\) (High performance tier). * Average \(3.0 – 3.49\): Scored as \(50\%\) (Satisfactory / baseline tier). * Average \(< 3.0\): No Value (\(0\%\)) (Unsatisfactory; no bonus; ineligible for vacancies). 4. Verified Bank Sign-Off Hierarchy: * No Self-Evaluation: Form format prepared and dispatched by the HR Performance Officer. * Evaluated by the Direct Supervisor / Assistant Branch Manager. * Countersigned by the Main Branch Manager / Unit Head. * Mandatory Employee Review: The employee views their evaluation and digitally signs it. 5. Direct Banking Outcomes: * Yearly Performance Bonus: Distributed directly based on the percentage score tier. * Internal Vacancy Competition: Serves as the primary competitive score for internal vacancies, enabling career advancement across classes (even enabling qualified Non-Clerical staff to compete for Clerical and Managerial posts).

Relational Data Model for MariaDB / Frappe Framework
1. Conceptual & Logical Data Model Overview
docs.text:
The Entity-Relationship (ER) Diagram formalizes the structural data foundation of LIBHRMS (anbesa_hr). It maps real-world commercial banking entities, attributes, primary keys (PK), foreign keys (FK), and cardinalities across 5 integrated functional domains:

  1. Core HR & Organizational Hierarchy:
  2. Reuses the legacy Employee ID (EmplID) for continuous audit provenance.
  3. Models the Department / Unit Tree (BusUnits) using Frappe's hierarchical NestedSet pattern.
  4. Supports M:N Guarantor relationships (one employee can have multiple guarantors, and a bank employee can act as a guarantor for multiple colleagues).
  5. Captures the 4-Tier Ethiopian Administrative Address (Region \(\rightarrow\) Zone \(\rightarrow\) Woreda \(\rightarrow\) Kebele).
  6. Leave Management & Ledger System:
  7. Implements the Immutable Leave Ledger (Leave_Ledger_Entry), permanently solving the Termination Officer's 2-week paper audit crisis.
  8. Reliever assignment and dual-calendar date tracking (Gregorian and Ethiopian Calendar timestamps).
  9. Payroll & Compensation Engine:
  10. Grid matrix linking Bank Pay Grade and Scale Step to Base Ethiopian Birr amounts.
  11. Detailed Salary_Slip capturing progressive Ethiopian income tax (ERCA), 7% employee pension, 11% bank pension liability, staff loan amortization, and leave reconciliation adjustments.
  12. Performance Appraisal Subsystem:
  13. Multi-template model supporting Managerial (15 questions), Clerical (11 questions), and Non-Clerical (14 Amharic questions).
  14. Itemized scoring table (scale 1 to 5) feeding into the converted discrete percentage bands (\(100\%, 75\%, 50\%, 0\%\)).
  15. Employee Separation & Exit Clearance (Proc. 1156/2019):
  16. Single-point 4-station Clearance Checklist (Branch, IT, Finance, Property).
  17. Automated settlement engine integrating severance rules (\(< 5\) yrs vs. \(\ge 5\) yrs) and reconciled leave encashment/recovery.

docs.title: 3. Key Relational Design Principles in this Schema
docs.text:
1. Provable Audit Lineage via Leave_Ledger_Entry:
  2. Instead of storing a vulnerable editable integer like remainLeaveDays, the system computes real-time leave balances using an immutable ledger.
  3. When an employee terminates, the system performs a query on SUM(days_credited) - SUM(days_debited) in milliseconds, permanently eliminating the 2-week archive crisis.
  4. Dynamic Performance Scoring Engine:
  5. Completely normalizes the questionnaire structure: Appraisal_Template \(\rightarrow\) Appraisal_Criteria \(\rightarrow\) Appraisal_Score_Detail.
  6. Directly supports Lion International Bank’s exact rule: 11 questions for Clerical, 14 in Amharic for Non-Clerical, and 15 for Managerial, with automatic mapping to the \(100\%, 75\%, 50\%, 0\%\) bands.
  7. M:N Guarantor Relationship (EMPLOYEE_GUARANTOR):

Formal Behavioral Logic for Complex Banking Computational Engines
1. Purpose & UML Modeling Context
docs.text:
While high-level business flowcharts model operational human handoffs across departments, UML Activity Diagrams model the internal algorithmic behavior, decision branching, mathematical calculations, and parallel concurrency executed by system services and database engines.

For LIBHRMS (anbesa_hr), this document provides the formal activity logic for the two most computationally complex banking engines: 1. Activity Diagram 1: Dual-Calendar Statutory Leave Accrual & Birr Encashment Engine: * Calculates tenure-based statutory annual leave accrual (\(16 + \lfloor\frac{\text{Years}}{2}\rfloor\)). * Executes dual-calendar synchronization (Gregorian GC \(\leftrightarrow\) Ethiopian EC). * Executes exact monetary valuation in Ethiopian Birr: \(\text{Daily Wage} = \frac{\text{Base}}{30} \times \text{Days}\). * Commits immutable debits/credits to tabLeave Ledger Entry. 2. Activity Diagram 2: Asynchronous Monthly Payroll Batch Execution & Statutory Deduction Engine: * Redis Queue background task dispatching. * Concurrent processing of banking allowances (Teller Cash Indemnity, Acting allowances, Transport). * Exact evaluation of the Ethiopian Ministry of Revenues (ERCA) 7-Tier Progressive Tax Schedule. * Computation of \(7\%\) employee pension and \(11\%\) bank expense liability. * Loan amortization deductions and automated compilation of the CBS Salary Batch Export File.

docs.title: 2. Activity Diagram 1: Dual-Calendar Leave Accrual & Birr Encashment Engine
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    %% =========================================================================
    %% ACTIVITY DIAGRAM 1: LEAVE ACCRUAL, EXPIRATION & BIDIRECTIONAL SETTLEMENT
    %% =========================================================================

    START([● Initial Node: Trigger Event]) --> CHECK_TRIGGER{"Trigger Type?"}

    %% Branch A: Fiscal Year Allocation & Expiration (Hamle 1)
    CHECK_TRIGGER -->|Annual Fiscal Run: Hamle 1| CALC_TENURE["Query tabEmployee.date_of_joining<br/>Calculate Total Banking Tenure in Months"]
    CALC_TENURE --> EVAL_SENIORITY["Calculate New Year Statutory Entitlement:<br/>Base = 16 Working Days<br/>Bonus = floor(Years of Service / 2) Days (Unlimited Increments)<br/>Current Year Entitlement = Base + Bonus"]

    EVAL_SENIORITY --> CHECK_EXPIRATION["<b>Evaluate 2-Year Expiration Rule (Proc. 1156/2019):</b><br/>Query Unused Leave older than 2 Fiscal Cycles (Year N - 2)"]
    CHECK_EXPIRATION --> HAS_EXPIRED{"Any Leave Older<br/>than 2 Years?"}

    HAS_EXPIRED -->|Yes| POST_EXPIRE["Post Forfeiture to tabLeave Ledger Entry:<br/>transaction_type = 'Expiration'<br/>leaves = -Expired_Days (Forfeited)"]
    HAS_EXPIRED -->|No| POST_ALLOC["Post Credit to tabLeave Ledger Entry:<br/>transaction_type = 'Allocation'<br/>leaves = +Current_Year_Days"]
    POST_EXPIRE --> POST_ALLOC
    POST_ALLOC --> STOP_ALLOC([◉ Activity Final: Allocation & Expiration Complete])

    %% Branch B: Exit Settlement (Termination Reconciliation)
    CHECK_TRIGGER -->|Termination Trigger: Exit Settlement| QUERY_BALANCE["Query tabLeave Ledger Entry for Employee:<br/>Reconciled Balance = SUM(leaves)"]
    QUERY_BALANCE --> CHECK_BAL_SIGN{"Reconciled Balance<br/>Positive or Negative?"}

    %% B1: Positive Balance
    CHECK_BAL_SIGN -->|Balance > 0 Positive| COMPUTE_ENCASH["<b>Positive Balance: Bank Pays Employee</b><br/>Daily Wage Rate = Base Salary / 30.00<br/>Encashment Earning (ETB) = Daily Rate × Unused Days"]
    COMPUTE_ENCASH --> POST_DEBIT_ENCASH["Post to tabLeave Ledger Entry:<br/>transaction_type = 'Encashment'<br/>leaves = -Unused_Days"]
    POST_DEBIT_ENCASH --> PUSH_PAY_EARN["Push to Final Settlement Slip:<br/><b>custom_leave_rec_etb = +Encashment (Taxable Earning)</b>"]
    PUSH_PAY_EARN --> STOP_POS([◉ Activity Final: Positive Encashment Added to Settlement])

    %% B2: Negative Balance
    CHECK_BAL_SIGN -->|Balance < 0 Negative| COMPUTE_RECOVERY["<b>Negative Balance: Employee Pays Bank</b><br/>Daily Wage Rate = Base Salary / 30.00<br/>Wage Recovery (ETB) = Daily Rate × abs(Negative Days)"]
    COMPUTE_RECOVERY --> POST_CREDIT_RECOVERY["Post to tabLeave Ledger Entry:<br/>transaction_type = 'Wage Recovery Settlement'<br/>leaves = +abs(Negative Days) (Balances Ledger to 0)"]

    PUSH_PAY_DEDUCT --> STOP_NEG([◉ Activity Final: Negative Recovery Deducted from Settlement])

    %% B3: Zero Balance
    CHECK_BAL_SIGN -->|Balance = 0 Neutral| ZERO_ADJ["Zero Adjustment: Leave is fully balanced"]
    ZERO_ADJ --> STOP_ZERO([◉ Activity Final: Zero Impact on Settlement])

flowchart TD
    %% =========================================================================
    %% ACTIVITY DIAGRAM 2: PAYROLL & PROGRESSIVE TAX ENGINE
    %% =========================================================================

    P_START([● Initial Node: Monthly Payroll Triggered]) --> P_INIT["Finance / HR Clicks 'Create Monthly Payroll Entry'<br/>Select Cutoff Period & Company"]
    P_INIT --> P_ENQUEUE["Enqueue Task into Redis Queue (RQ):<br/><code>anbesa_hr.payroll.process_batch(payroll_entry)</code>"]

    P_WORKER --> P_QUERY_STAFF["Query all active staff (status = 'Permanent' or 'Probationary')<br/>Initialize Process Loop (Iterate Staff)"]

    P_QUERY_STAFF --> LOOP_START{"More Staff<br/>in Batch?"}

    %% Staff Processing Pipeline (Fork / Concurrent Evaluation)
    LOOP_START -->|Yes: Next Employee| FORK_START[["== FORK: Concurrent Earnings Collation =="]]

    FORK_START --> COMP_BASE["1. Base Pay per Active Grade & Step Assignment"]
    FORK_START --> COMP_ALLOW["2. Banking Allowances:<br/>• Cash Indemnity (if teller)<br/>• Acting Allowance (if acting)<br/>• Housing / Representation"]
    FORK_START --> COMP_LEAVE_ADJ["3. Leave Ledger Adjustments:<br/>• (+) Approved Encashment ETB<br/>• (-) Unpaid LWP Days × (Base/30)"]

    COMP_TAXABLE --> ERCA_BRACKET{"Evaluate Taxable Income<br/>against ERCA Progressive Brackets"}

    ERCA_BRACKET -->|0 to 600 ETB| TAX_T1["Tax Rate = 0% | Deduct 0 ETB"]
    ERCA_BRACKET -->|601 to 1,650 ETB| TAX_T2["Tax = (Taxable × 10%) - 60.00 ETB"]
    ERCA_BRACKET -->|1,651 to 3,200 ETB| TAX_T3["Tax = (Taxable × 15%) - 142.50 ETB"]
    ERCA_BRACKET -->|3,201 to 5,250 ETB| TAX_T4["Tax = (Taxable × 20%) - 302.50 ETB"]
    ERCA_BRACKET -->|5,251 to 7,800 ETB| TAX_T5["Tax = (Taxable × 25%) - 565.00 ETB"]
    ERCA_BRACKET -->|7,801 to 10,900 ETB| TAX_T6["Tax = (Taxable × 30%) - 955.00 ETB"]
    ERCA_BRACKET -->|> 10,900 ETB| TAX_T7["Tax = (Taxable × 35%) - 1,500.00 ETB"]

    TAX_T1 --> CONSOLIDATE_TAX["Consolidate Total Income Tax (ERCA)"]
    TAX_T2 --> CONSOLIDATE_TAX
    TAX_T3 --> CONSOLIDATE_TAX
    TAX_T4 --> CONSOLIDATE_TAX
    TAX_T5 --> CONSOLIDATE_TAX
    TAX_T6 --> CONSOLIDATE_TAX
    TAX_T7 --> CONSOLIDATE_TAX

    %% Pension & Loans
    CONSOLIDATE_TAX --> COMP_PENSION["Calculate Statutory Pension Scheme:<br/>• Staff Pension (7%) = Base Salary × 0.07<br/>• Bank Liability (11%) = Base Salary × 0.11"]
    COMP_PENSION --> COMP_LOANS["Fetch Active Staff Loan Amortization Cuts<br/>(Monthly Principal + Interest Deductions)"]
    COMP_LOANS --> COMP_NET["Compute Net Pay:<br/>Net Pay = Gross Pay - (Tax + 7% Pension + Loans)"]

    COMP_NET --> SAVE_SLIP["Insert / Update tabSalary Slip<br/>Set bank_ac_no, docstatus = 0 (Draft)"]
    SAVE_SLIP --> LOOP_START

    GEN_CBS_FILE --> NOTIFY_MAKER["Send Desk Notification to Payroll Officer & Finance Director:<br/>'Monthly Payroll Batch Calculated Successfully'"]

docs.title: 1. The ERCA Progressive Tax Algorithm
docs.text:
In Ethiopian commercial banking, calculating personal income tax is mathematically non-linear. The Activity Diagram specifies the standard marginal tax equation: $\(\text{Tax Payable} = (\text{Taxable Income} \times \text{Bracket Rate}) - \text{Statutory Deduction Constant}\)$

Monthly Taxable Income (ETB) Marginal Rate Statutory Constant (ETB) \(0 \text{ to } 600\) \(0\%\) \(0.00\) \(601 \text{ to } 1,650\) \(10\%\) \(60.00\) \(1,651 \text{ to } 3,200\) \(15\%\) \(142.50\) \(3,201 \text{ to } 5,250\) \(20\%\) \(302.50\) \(5,251 \text{ to } 7,800\) \(25\%\) \(565.00\) \(7,801 \text{ to } 10,900\) \(30\%\) \(955.00\) Over \(10,900\) \(35\%\) \(1,500.00\)

docs.title: 2. Fork/Join Concurrency in Earnings
docs.text: The worker thread executes a UML Fork to evaluate base pay, dynamic allowances (Cash Indemnity, Acting, Representation), and leave adjustments independently before a Join node aggregates total gross compensation. This architecture eliminates sequential calculation bottlenecks for large branch payroll runs.

docs.title: Executive Summary & Modernization Objectives
docs.text:
This document provides the formal System Design Document (SDD) and technical architecture blueprint for modernizing the human capital and payroll operations of Lion International Bank S.C. (LIB).

The initiative migrates legacy operations from a fragmented, static desktop-era database (HRADMINDB) to a centralized, web-based enterprise platform (anbesa_hr).

docs.title: Core Business Objectives Addressed:
docs.text:
1. Permanent Resolution of the 2-Week Leave Archive Nightmare: Replaces manual searches across dusty branch paper archives and disconnected Head Office Excel spreadsheets with a real-time, immutable Leave Ledger Entry engine that calculates certified audit balances in 1 millisecond.
  2. Statutory Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019 Enforcement: Automates the Rolling 2-Year Leave Expiration Policy and tenure-based severance calculations (\(< 5\) years service = 0 ETB; \(\ge 5\) years service = statutory formula).
  3. Official 24-Section Employee Profile Form Parity: Mirrors all 24 sections of Lion Bank's physical registration dossier (including dual-calendar birth dates, anti-nepotism audit checks, and nationwide mobility pledges).
  4. Bilingual Performance Appraisal & Bonus Linkage: Automates the 11-question (Clerical), 14-question (Non-Clerical in Amharic), and 15-question (Managerial) evaluations with mathematical score conversion into \(100\%, 75\%, 50\%, 0\%\) tiers for annual bonus distribution and internal vacancy promotions.
  5. Decoupled Downstream Core Banking Handover: Generates standardized, verified CBS Salary Batch Export Files for manual credit to employee accounts via Core Banking (Temenos T24 / Finacle).

docs.title: 1. System Boundaries & High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
The system operates strictly within the Lion International Bank Private Intranet / Domain, isolated behind corporate firewalls. External web entry is managed by an Nginx reverse proxy terminating SSL on standard ports (443/80), which accelerates static media and routes dynamic traffic to the Frappe application runtime (Python WSGI). Heavy computations are offloaded to Redis Queue (RQ) background workers, while data is persisted in MariaDB Enterprise (InnoDB utf8mb4).

docs.title: 2. Module & Component Architecture (C4 Level 3)
docs.text:
The application layer decomposes into 5 cohesive business subsystems plus shared banking utilities: * Core HR Master (anbesa_hr): Employee dossier, 4-tier Ethiopian address, fidelity guarantor records, and exit clearance checklist. * Leave Management: Accrual rules, reliever endorsements, dual-calendar balances, and Birr encashment calculations. * Payroll & Compensation: Pay Grade + Scale Step matrix, allowances (Cash Indemnity, Acting), progressive ERCA income tax, and pension liabilities. * Performance Appraisal: 3-tier questionnaire catalogs, double supervisory sign-off, and bonus/vacancy linkage. * Training History: Academic records, certifications, and service bonding agreements. * Shared Utilities: Ethiopian Calendar (EC \(\leftrightarrow\) GC) translation engine, secure Document Media Vault, and notification dispatcher.

docs.title: 3. Functional Scope & Use-Case Model
docs.text:
To eliminate role confusion and preserve software modularity, the functional scope is modeled using UML Actor Generalization: * Universal Base Role: Every user in the bank (Branch Manager, HR Officer, Finance Officer, IT Admin) inherits baseline Employee Self-Service (ESS) capabilities (viewing payslips, applying for leave, and reviewing appraisals). * Specialized Operational Realms: Decomposed into non-overlapping packages: (1) Self-Service & Branch Operations, (2) HR Operations & Personnel Lifecycle, and (3) Compensation & System Governance.

docs.title: 4. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) & Governance Matrix
docs.text:
In compliance with National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) governance and external audit standards, access control enforces the Two-Man Rule (Maker-Checker) and branch-level row security: * The Maker (Preparer): Drafts records (docstatus = 0). Cannot authorize their own submission. * The Checker (Authorizer): Formally reviews, verifies General Ledger/policy compliance, and commits (docstatus = 1). * Deletion Lockdown: Physical Delete (D) permissions are locked down on financial, leave ledger, and personnel records to ensure an immutable audit trail.

docs.title: 5.1 End-to-End Employee Lifecycle Flow
docs.text:
Governs the staff journey across 4 audited phases: 1. Recruitment & 24-Section Form Onboarding: Candidate fills paper form with a pen; file is verified and bound; HR Data Encoder enters data into anbesa_hr (mandatory core fields vs. optional child tables). 2. 45-Day Statutory Probation & Guarantor Gate: Confirmation to permanent status requires verified personal guarantors and signed liability undertakings recorded in employee_guarantor. 3. Career Operations: Lateral branch transfers (preserving pay scale) and merit promotions (updating pay grade and hr_emp_salary). 4. Separation & Exit Clearance (Labour Proc. 1156/2019): Single 4-point checklist (Branch, IT, Finance, Property); instant 1-second Leave Ledger reconciliation; automated severance pay (\(< 5\) yrs = 0 ETB; \(\ge 5\) yrs = statutory formula); and 1-click Certificate of Service generation.

docs.title: 5.2 Dual-Calendar Leave Management Flow
docs.text:
• Seniority Accrual: Computes statutory baseline (\(16 \text{ days} + 1 \text{ day per 2 years of service}\)) aligned with the Ethiopian fiscal year (Hamle 1 – Sene 30).
  • Reliever Handover Endorsement: Branch tellers/cashiers cannot depart on leave without a designated reliever formally accepting cash drawer, vault key, and client responsibilities.
  • Rolling 2-Year Leave Expiration Policy: Unutilized leave older than two fiscal cycles expires automatically per Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019.
  • Bidirectional Exit Settlement: Reconciled balance feeds into final settlement: Positive balance \(\rightarrow\) Encashment Earning in Birr; Negative balance \(\rightarrow\) Wage Recovery Deduction paid back to the bank.

docs.text:
• Multi-Source Input Collation: Dynamic collation of base salaries, branch allowances (Teller Cash Indemnity, Acting allowances, Transport), and leave adjustments (LWP cuts or encashment earnings).

  • Statutory Deductions: 7-tier ERCA progressive personal income tax, 7% employee pension, 11% bank pension liability, and loan amortization deductions.
